protocol:
1. Put on blue nitrile gloves and set up labeled 0.2 mL PCR tubes in a green tube rack on the laboratory bench.

2. Open a pipette tip box and attach a disposable tip to an adjustable micropipette set to 10 µL.

3. Pipette liquid into the first labeled 0.2 mL PCR tube held in the green rack.

4. Return the filled PCR tube to the green rack beside the other labeled tubes.

5. Pick up a second labeled 0.2 mL PCR tube from the rack and pipette liquid into it with the 10 µL micropipette.

6. Place the second filled PCR tube back into the green rack.

7. Attach a fresh disposable tip to the micropipette from the open tip box.

8. Pick up another labeled PCR tube and pipette liquid into the tube using the 10 µL micropipette.

9. Return the filled PCR tube to the green rack with the other prepared tubes.

10. Repeat pipetting liquid into additional labeled 0.2 mL PCR tubes using the adjustable micropipette and disposable tips.

11. Close the caps on the prepared PCR tubes by pressing the attached tube lids shut.

12. Carry the capped PCR tubes from the bench to the centrifuge and thermocycler area.

13. Open the lid of the mini centrifuge and handle the prepared PCR tubes near the rotor area.

14. Move the capped PCR tubes from the centrifuge area to the thermal cycler.

15. Open the heated lid of the thermal cycler to expose the PCR block.

16. Insert the capped 0.2 mL PCR tubes into wells of the thermal cycler block.

17. Close the heated lid of the thermal cycler over the loaded PCR tubes.
